To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the digestibility of crude energy and protein decreased when BPM was increased in the diet of growing mink kits, but the nitrogen retention and the heat production remained unaffected.
the digestible protein content of BPM was lower than that of fish meal and that the digestible energy content was higher.
The digestibility of energy and protein decreased with increased inclusion of BPM.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new feed ingredient, bacterial protein meal (bpm), produced from waste biomass and natural gas in a biogas plant, and the use of bpm as an ingredient in the diet of growing mink kits, and the effects on energy and protein utilization in the animals.
the effect of increasing dietary BPM on energy and protein utilization in growing mink.
the effect of increasing dietary content of BPM on energy and protein retention in mink.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of BPM as a protein source in mink feed can reduce feed costs without compromising animal health or production.
a diet containing up to 40–50% of DN derived from BPM can be recommended in growing mink diets.

the mink kits fed 40% of the digested N derived from BPM had a lower feed intake, a lower apparent digestibility of protein and energy and a lower retained energy compared with kits fed a diet with 20% of the digester N derived from BPM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mink can utilize the energy in BPM to a high degree.
BPM can be used as a substitute for fish meal in mink diets without any adverse effects on energy and protein utilization.
the use of BPM in diets for growing mink is feasible up to 40%, and that it can be used in a similar way as other protein sources, such as fish meal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BPM is a good protein substitute in diets for growing mink, but that the inclusion level should not be higher than 40% of the DN.
the mink kits were able to adapt to the diets with increasing proportions of BPM, which was reflected by unchanged heat production and nitrogen balance.
it is possible to replace 40% of the DN in the diet of growing mink kits with a bacterial protein meal produced using natural gas.
